result.title: From Code to Playable Systems: CEGame-Bench for Long-Horizon Game Creation Agents
result.summary: A game ships when a player can launch it, finish it, and return to a saved world, none of which a successful build guarantees, yet game-creation agents are mostly tested on one engine or on one-prompt browser games. We present CEGame-Bench, the first long-horizon benchmark for complete-game creation across five production engines: Defold, Godot, Roblox Studio, Unity, and Unreal Engine. Agents build each game from an empty project and a design document in runs averaging up to 295 steps and 65M tokens; the document doubles as a contract, and a hidden evaluator accepts a game only by real-input play. Under four scaffolds, agents earn most integration points but usually under half the gameplay points, and their games reach the ending in only 16% of runs, while references built by engineers with coding agents score near the maximum, which places this artifact-to-play gap in the agents. No two engines rank configurations alike (Kendall's tau 0.14-0.62), and the same game usually scores higher on Unity and Unreal Engine, which check more before play. We release Game Completion Boost, an agent skill for requirement-driven playtesting and repair that raises the execution-based score of three models by 14.1-24.3 points.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 CEGame-Bench，跨五个游戏引擎的长时程「完整游戏创建」基准：智能体从空工程和设计文档出发（单次运行可达数百步、数千万 token），由隐藏评估器以真实输入试玩来判定成败，并发布要求驱动的试玩与修复 skill（Game Completion Boost）。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「能构建、却不可玩」的评估缺口与要求驱动的试玩—修复循环，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正参与最终输出、以及把验证纳入训练监督提供方法线索，需人工核查其验证-修复机制的可迁移性。
